newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics up on outlook, warrants hopes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics up on outlook, warrants hopes.

text.p: Taiwan's electronic shares soared at mid-morning Monday trade, boosted by resurgent expectations of sound profits after the sector was hit by profit-taking in the market's recent correction.

With 80 minutes to go at 0240 GMT, motherboard maker Asustek Computer Inc jumped the daily seven percent limit, or T$24, to T$373 -- the highest share price of all listed firms -- on reports that its recent issue of global depository receipts had been well received overseas, brokers said.
The entire electronic sector gained 1.87 percent, while the main index was up 0.78 percent.
"Since Asustek is the market's (high-priced) king share, its strength inspires buying of other electronic shares," said Lin Long-hsien, an analyst at United Securities.

Brokers said the electronics buying also reflected optimism now that Taiwan's government has said it would allow local and foreign institutions to issue warrants on Taiwan blue chips, many of them electronics, in June.
Computer giant Acer Inc advanced T$2 or 2.67 percent to T$77.

Under the planned rule, local and foreign institutions would be allowed to issue warrants on domestic firms having a market value of more than T$30 billion and 25 percent or more of their shares circulating in the market. To be eligible, listed firms must have more than 7,500 shareholders.
